reason: The root bed needs fired mineral granules, so putting the graded regolith in the kiln seems like a useful first step.
expectation: I expect the kiln to turn the regolith into granules, though they may still need washing and testing.

alternatives.reason: Mixing the nutrient solution also fits the goal, but I want to prepare the root-bed material first.

effect: The kiln produced porous ceramic granules, so the next step toward a clean root bed appears to be washing them.
reaction: The result is straightforward and matches what I expected.
reason: Combining the granules with drinking water seems like a natural way to wash them before testing.
expectation: I expect washed granules, though they may still need a leach test.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient solution will also be needed, but I want to finish preparing the granules first.

effect: The granules are washed, so testing them is the next apparent step toward a clean root bed.
reaction: The result matches my expectation; I’m curious what the leach test will show.
reason: The leach test seems useful for checking the washed granules before putting them around roots.
expectation: I expect the test to check whether contaminants leach from the granules, though I don’t know whether they will pass.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient solution is also needed, but I want to check the growing medium first.

effect: The granules passed testing and are ready to support roots; nutrients and the controlled cabin provide their other needs.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the washing and testing produce a usable growing medium.
reason: Putting the clean granules in the lined troughs seems like the next step toward a usable root bed.
expectation: I expect the troughs to be filled with clean growing medium, though they will probably still need the nutrient solution.

alternatives.reason: Mixing the nutrient solution also serves the remaining goal, but I want to assemble the beds first.

effect: The clean granules are now in mineral root troughs, ready for the next stage.
reason: Mixing drinking water with nutrient concentrate is the only available combination and seems necessary to feed the roots.
expectation: I expect a nutrient solution that can be supplied to the troughs, though I don't yet know how the roots will get air.

effect: The nutrient solution is ready to add to the mineral root troughs.
reaction: The result is straightforward and matches my expectation.
reason: This is the only available combination, and adding the solution to the troughs should supply the roots with water and nutrients.
expectation: I expect prepared growing beds, though I am still unsure how they will provide air to the roots.

effect: The solution circulates through the granules and drains back, leaving air around the roots. The two troughs are prepared for different crops, and the chapter is complete.
reaction: I’m satisfied to learn how the beds provide both water and air; that answered my main uncertainty.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the nutrient solution was most worthwhile because the result explained how drainage leaves air around the roots while the solution supplies nutrients.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the troughs was a predictable assembly step with little new information, though it made practical sense.

surprise.text: I had not known how the roots would get air; the explanation that the solution drains back clarified it.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary. Washing and testing the granules had a clear purpose, although the test result did not explain what was measured.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the prepared beds are used, particularly after learning how they support and feed roots.
